Pilot partners & family

10 anniversary gifts for couples who love aviation

An anniversary gift works best when the aviation connection belongs to both of you. Think about a trip, a place or a shared ritual before choosing an aircraft-shaped object. These ideas range from simple keepsakes to experiences you can plan together.

By Pilot Gift Guide Updated 2026-10-20

How we choose our recommendations
In this guideThe ideasHow to chooseMore gift ideas

The ideas

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    A framed map of your first trip

    Mark the places you actually visited and add a short personal caption. Decorative maps need not be operational charts, and a clean design will usually age better.

  2. 2

    A photo book organized by journeys

    Include the ordinary moments as well as the impressive views. A few sentences about each trip make the book more personal than pages of uncaptioned airport photographs.

  3. 3

    An airport-view dinner

    Choose somewhere with a view both partners will enjoy. Confirm the venue is publicly accessible and make the meal, rather than aircraft spotting alone, the center of the evening.

  4. 4

    A model of an anniversary-trip aircraft

    This works when a particular aircraft is part of your story. Verify the type and airline before commissioning personalization or choosing a collectible model.

  5. 5

    A flexible weekend away

    Agree on a destination together and keep the booking terms practical. The gift is time together; it should not depend on a difficult standby or work-schedule assumption.

  6. 6

    A paired travel-journal set

    Choose journals that fit how each person records memories. Add a first entry about an earlier trip rather than leaving both books entirely blank.

  7. 7

    A museum day with a special meal

    Combine an aviation collection with a restaurant or neighborhood you both want to explore. Leave enough time that the day does not feel like a tight connection.

  8. 8

    A commissioned illustration of a shared place

    An airport, coastline or destination can be more distinctive than a generic airplane drawing. Ask to approve the composition before the artist produces the final work.

  9. 9

    A home build night

    Choose a model or building set that you both want to assemble. Clear a table, plan the evening and think ahead about where the finished result will live.

  10. 10

    A letter about the next journey

    Include a realistic plan you can act on together. Avoid a vague promise of travel that leaves all the organizing to the recipient.

How to choose

Use the shared story as the selection rule. If one partner enjoys aviation much more than the other, pair that interest with a destination, meal or activity both want. Protect the celebration from schedule changes with realistic travel time and flexible reservations.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
